name: Tamsulosin
route_note: Oral modified-release capsule or tablet once daily
owner: generic (many); Boehringer Ingelheim (Flomax, US) and Astellas

discovery.note: A sulfonamide alpha-blocker selective for the alpha1A subtype that predominates in prostate smooth muscle.

tagline: Uroselective alpha blocker that eases urinary symptoms of prostate enlargement
summary: Tamsulosin selectively blocks alpha1A and alpha1D adrenoceptors in the prostate and bladder neck, relaxing smooth muscle and improving urine flow. It is one of the most prescribed drugs for lower urinary tract symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia.
mechanism: Noradrenaline acting on alpha1A receptors contracts smooth muscle in the prostate, prostatic urethra and bladder neck. Tamsulosin blocks these receptors, reducing outlet resistance and improving flow and symptoms.

Its relative selectivity over alpha1B receptors in blood vessels causes less hypotension than older alpha blockers such as prazosin, so it does not need dose titration. Blockade of alpha1A receptors in the iris dilator muscle causes intraoperative floppy iris syndrome.
uses: Lower urinary tract symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia
Facilitating passage of distal ureteric stones (off-label)

history.title: Japanese approval
history.detail: Tamsulosin is approved in Japan as Harnal.

history.title: Floppy iris syndrome
history.detail: Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome during cataract surgery is described in tamsulosin users.

history.title: Generics and combination
history.detail: Generic tamsulosin launches in the US; dutasteride/tamsulosin (Jalyn) is approved; Flomax Relief becomes available from UK pharmacies.

history.title: Ureteric stones trial
history.detail: The SUSPEND trial finds no benefit of tamsulosin for passage of ureteric stones overall.

facts: Patients planning cataract surgery are advised to tell their eye surgeon about tamsulosin use.
Tamsulosin is often combined with a 5α-reductase inhibitor such as dutasteride or finasteride.
